It's interesting because the location information given from the diagnostic is not really very useful:

```
/tmp/mhlo_repro_cleaned.mlir:6:10: error: 'flow.ex.stream.fragment' op constant subspan op was mapped to multiple buffer ranges while allocating transient buffers
    %3 = "mhlo.compare"(%arg0, %2) {comparison_direction = "GT"} : (tensor<1x4xf32>, tensor<1x4xf32>) -> tensor<1x4xi1>

```

> It's interesting because the location information given from the diagnostic is not really very useful:

I've realized this is because the stream op has a fused location and the diagnostic handler only prints out the first one

Ok I was finally able to reduce the repro from the original mhlo mlir through various iterative removals followed by cleanup passes:


```mlir
  func @main(%arg0: tensor<4x1x11x2xf32>) -> tensor<4x8x11x2xf32> attributes {iree.module.export} {
    %0 = mhlo.constant dense<0.000000e+00> : tensor<4x8x11x2xf32>
    %1 = mhlo.constant dense<1.000000e+00> : tensor<4x1x11x2xf32>
    %2 = mhlo.constant dense<0> : tensor<i32>
    %3 = mhlo.multiply %arg0, %1 : tensor<4x1x11x2xf32>
    %4 = "mhlo.dynamic-update-slice"(%0, %3, %2, %2, %2, %2) : (tensor<4x8x11x2xf32>, tensor<4x1x11x2xf32>, tensor<i32>, tensor<i32>, tensor<i32>, tensor<i32>) -> tensor<4x8x11x2xf32>
    return %4 : tensor<4x8x11x2xf32>
  }
```

```shell
$ iree-opt --iree-hal-target-backends=dylib-llvm-aot --iree-transformation-pipeline repro.mlir
```

So as I suspected, the heart of this problem is the mhlo.dynamic-update-slice. So this is a local reproducer that actually comes from the above example (not the one generated by the MLIR reproducer generation because that one includes a bunch of unrelated goop.

```mlir
  // configuration: -pass-pipeline='iree-convert-to-hal'
  func @main(%arg0: tensor<4x1x11x2xf32>) -> tensor<4x8x11x2xf32> attributes {iree.module.export, iree.reflection = {f = "I14!B10!d4d1d11d2R14!B10!d4d8d11d2", fv = "1"}} {
    %0 = flow.ex.stream.fragment(%arg0) : (tensor<4x1x11x2xf32>) -> tensor<4x8x11x2xf32> =
        (%arg1: tensor<4x1x11x2xf32>) -> tensor<4x8x11x2xf32> {
      %c2 = constant 2 : index
      %c11 = constant 11 : index
      %c4 = constant 4 : index
      %c32 = constant 32 : index
      %const_span = hal.constant.subspan @_const_pool_splats[#hal.byte_range<0, 2816>] : tensor<4x8x11x2xf32>
      %1 = flow.tensor.reshape %arg1 : tensor<4x1x11x2xf32> -> tensor<4x11x2xf32>
      %2 = flow.dispatch @main_dispatch_0::@main_dispatch_0[%c2, %c11, %c4](%1) {hal.bindings = [#hal.ex.operand_buffer<"s0b0_ro_external", 0 : index>, #hal.ex.result_buffer<"s0b1_xw_external", 0 : index>]} : (tensor<4x11x2xf32>) -> tensor<4x11x2xf32>
      %3 = flow.dispatch @main_dispatch_1::@main_dispatch_1[%c2, %c11, %c32](%2, %const_span) {hal.bindings = [#hal.ex.constant_storage<"s0b0_ro_constant", "_const_pool_splats", 0 : index, 2816 : index>, #hal.ex.operand_buffer<"s0b1_ro_external", 0 : index>]} : (tensor<4x11x2xf32>, tensor<4x8x11x2xf32>) -> %const_span
      flow.return %3 : tensor<4x8x11x2xf32>
    }
    return %0 : tensor<4x8x11x2xf32>
  }
```
Ah sorry I forgot to note that the above repro is with Hanhan's changes patched in (lowering mhlo.dynamic-update-slice to linalg on tensors). That's why it's a dispatch now, I'd guess.

The same initial mhlo triggers the same issue without that patch as well. In this case the local reproducer is

```mlir
  // configuration: -pass-pipeline='iree-convert-to-hal'
  func @main(%arg0: tensor<4x1x11x2xf32>) -> tensor<4x8x11x2xf32> attributes {iree.module.export, iree.reflection = {f = "I14!B10!d4d1d11d2R14!B10!d4d8d11d2", fv = "1"}} {
    %0 = flow.ex.stream.fragment(%arg0) : (tensor<4x1x11x2xf32>) -> tensor<4x8x11x2xf32> =
        (%arg1: tensor<4x1x11x2xf32>) -> tensor<4x8x11x2xf32> {
      %c2 = constant 2 : index
      %c11 = constant 11 : index
      %c4 = constant 4 : index
      %c0 = constant 0 : index
      %const_span = hal.constant.subspan @_const_pool_splats[#hal.byte_range<0, 2816>] : tensor<4x8x11x2xf32>
      %1 = flow.tensor.reshape %arg1 : tensor<4x1x11x2xf32> -> tensor<4x11x2xf32>
      %2 = flow.dispatch @main_dispatch_0::@main_dispatch_0[%c2, %c11, %c4](%1) {hal.bindings = [#hal.ex.operand_buffer<"s0b0_ro_external", 0 : index>, #hal.ex.result_buffer<"s0b1_xw_external", 0 : index>]} : (tensor<4x11x2xf32>) -> tensor<4x11x2xf32>
      %3 = flow.tensor.reshape %2 : tensor<4x11x2xf32> -> tensor<4x1x11x2xf32>
      %4 = flow.tensor.update %3, %const_span[%c0, %c0, %c0, %c0] : tensor<4x1x11x2xf32> -> tensor<4x8x11x2xf32>
      flow.return %4 : tensor<4x8x11x2xf32>
    }
    return %0 : tensor<4x8x11x2xf32>
  }
```
It really doesn't make sense that we'd be doing an update into a constant span. Seems like trying to write into that is both bad and is what's causing the issue here.

@rsuderman am I remembering right that you looked at dynamic-update-slice at some point? It looks like somewhere in the pipeline we're trying to overwrite an existing tensor which doesn't work with the value semantics. I have a vague recollection of us arguing about this before :stuck_out_tongue: (sorry if I'm misremembering).

https://www.tensorflow.org/xla/operation_semantics#dynamicupdateslice definitely implies value semantics to me.

Obviously at some point in the pipeline we should realize that that constant is only ever used for one thing, that it's a splat, and that it's getting overwritten so the whole thing shouldn't be externed into some constant pool at all.

In fact, in this particular case I think the dynamic-update-slice could be converted to a pad operation, since the constant is a splat: https://www.tensorflow.org/xla/operation_semantics#pad. But IMO that's also just working around some other issues we have here

It's not clear to me whether conversion of an `mhlo.dynamic-update-slice` to an `mhlo.pad` would be considered a candidate for a canonicalization, but I think it might be a pattern we want and we could add it to [HLOToHLOPreprocessing](https://github.com/google/iree/blob/main/iree/compiler/Dialect/Flow/Transforms/HLOToHLOPreprocessing.cpp). Again this is just a workaround for what is fundamentally at least one bug in the compiler, but given that we're trying to delete all the stream stuff in the next month or so, it might be an OK workaround. A pattern that does something like:

```mlir
%target = mhlo.constant dense<0.000000e+00> : tensor<4x8x11x2xf32>
%1 = mhlo.constant dense<0> : tensor<i32>
%2 = "mhlo.dynamic-update-slice"(%target, %update, %1, %1, %1, %1) : (tensor<4x8x11x2xf32>, tensor<4x1x11x2xf32>, tensor<i32>, tensor<i32>, tensor<i32>, tensor<i32>) -> tensor<4x8x11x2xf32>
```
->
```mlir
%c0 = mhlo.constant dense<0.000000e+00> : tensor<f32>
%1 = "mhlo.pad"(%update, %c0) {
    edge_padding_low = dense<0> : tensor<4xi64>,
    edge_padding_high = dense<[0, 7, 0, 0]> : tensor<4xi64>,
    interior_padding = dense<0> : tensor<4xi64>
} : (tensor<4x8x11x2xf32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<4x8x11x2xf32>
```

Could also be a more generic lowering to an `mhlo.dynamic_pad` which then already has canonicalizations to get canonicalized to a pad, but I think the value prop is maybe less clear if you have to do math on all the padding dimensions.
Lei seems like you've figured out a fix for this while I was out? I should go on vacation more often :grin:

Shhh, don't tell anyone. 😊  I was hitting the same issue when addressing a new segfault after rebasing https://github.com/google/iree/pull/5614 to the top of the tree. Let me address comments and try to get the fix landed.
https://github.com/google/iree/pull/6174 should address this. @GMNGeoffrey please verify and close the issue.


issue.body:
Constants are collected together into a pool. They already have
their own buffer that is read only. When converting to HAL
we analyze `flow.ex.stream.fragment` ops and their regions to
allocate output/transient buffers. The buffer allocation there
considers aliasing. But we cannot create aliases from constant
subspans if they are mutated. We need to allocate new buffers
and copy over the data for mutated cases.
